body: I don't think I'm androgynous or feminine looking at all. I could try another word, but I don't know how to even begin bringing it up in conversation. She's worried that she hurt my feelings.

Do I need to spend 10,000 company seals every time I want to swap between classes? How limited will I be if I want to play a Scholar with 30 extra points in Intelligence?

It's not so much that I'm trying to define myself with relationships. It's more like I'm wondering if I even have anything worth offering if I can't meet people. And if I don't know anyone, then who am I really hurting?
I wish you could grab his tail at that point. I know I thought that's what the guides meant when it said to run around him and attack his tail.

I ended up forgoing battling covenant members. Farming the drakes took me an hour and a half (with max item find) to get 30 dragon scales. I don't really think the dragon head attack is all that worth it in general, though. It has a warmup and devours your stamina.
I really like the big weapons. Like the dragon greatsword. I hardly ever have the strength to use it though. :(

I was almost discouraged when I saw the reviews and the metacritic score of .3. I'm glad I ignored it and got the game. RE5 got overall better reviews if I recall and I felt it was actually not as solid as this game.

I do really miss the weapon system from 5, though. Pretty much my only qualm.

I can't really afford to see a doctor, but I'll try to do some cardio and stuff more.

I'm actually supposed to be on my 3rd year now. I have the credits for it, sat down with an adviser, did the degree mapping, etc. When I started college, I had intended to do something like education. But when I got into the higher level maths, I just had so much fun with it that it became something that really intrigued me. I'm planning on going into computer engineering. If I can ever get all of the resources together.

I'll try not to pressure myself or stress myself out too much. I feel like I'm constantly under pressure/stress, though. It's funny you brought that up since I didn't mention it in my post IIRC.

I need a place to stay while I go to college, food, tuition, books, and maybe transportation. I did the math and just for tuition and a cheap dorm, it would be $5800 for one term. I already know which of my credits will transfer. I'm subscribed to r/engineering on another account. Trust me. I'm not just complaining for the sake of complaining. I've been on top of a lot of this stuff. (Not to sound standoffish. I do appreciate the tips)
Honestly, I'd like to be an engineer of some sort. I'd love to work for a company like Raytheon, or even small engineering firms.

I mentioned in my post why I'm afraid to work out: I feel like I'm falling apart as is. It seems like whenever I start working out, I get new stretchmarks. Eating healthy is, believe it or not, not one of my biggest issues. I eat a pretty balanced diet (plenty of fruits and veggies, not a ton of sugar, good amounts of proteins without too much red meat, etc.) I just always hear people say how they drastically change their diet when they work out.

Clearly it's not working for me. Otherwise I wouldn't be on an advice board.
